en: Mayon Volcano in Albay features a nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape that is clearly visible from surrounding towns.
The Pasig River in Metro Manila naturally flows in a northwest direction from Laguna de Bay toward Manila Bay.
During the amihan season from December to February, the Philippines experiences cool and dry northeast winds.
The grass-covered Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn chocolate brown during the dry season, giving the landmark its famous name.
Taal Lake in Batangas is unique because it is a large freshwater lake situated entirely inside the Taal Volcano caldera.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Hikers climbing Mount Pulag in Benguet often observe a famous sea of clouds phenomenon hovering above the mountain peak at sunrise.
The Philippine tarsier, native to Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its entire brain.
Maria Cristina Falls in Lanao del Norte consists of two distinct waterfalls dropping simultaneously into a deep, rocky gorge.
The famous White Beach in Boracay is made of fine, powdery white sand composed primarily of crushed coral and shells.
A large, deep crater lake now fills the caldera of Mount Pinatubo in Zambales following its massive 1991 eruption.
Baguio City experiences significantly lower average temperatures than Manila because it is located at a high elevation in the Cordillera mountains.
